\# ADR-0001: SeniorITa AI Agent Governance Architecture



\## Status



Accepted



\## Date



2026-07-29



\## Context



SeniorITa introduces a governed multi-agent AI engineering framework.



The project requires a structured approach to coordinate specialized AI agents while maintaining:



\- architectural consistency

\- security validation

\- software quality

\- documentation integrity

\- operational reliability



Without governance, AI assisted development can introduce:



\- inconsistent decisions

\- duplicated implementations

\- security risks

\- undocumented architectural changes



\## Decision



SeniorITa adopts a centralized AI governance model based on:



\- AI Orchestrator Agent

\- Specialized AI Agents

\- Governance Rules

\- Knowledge Management Layer

\- Automated Validation Workflow



The Orchestrator Agent becomes the coordination layer responsible for:



\- request analysis

\- agent selection

\- workflow execution

\- governance enforcement



\## Agent Architecture



The system is composed of:



\### Coordination Layer



\- orchestrator agent



\### Architecture Layer



\- architect agent



Responsibilities:



\- system design

\- dependency analysis

\- architecture decisions





\### Development Layer



\- developer agent



Responsibilities:



\- implementation

\- refactoring

\- feature development





\### Quality Layer



\- test agent

\- reviewer agent



Responsibilities:



\- testing

\- regression validation

\- code quality analysis





\### Security Layer



\- security agent



Responsibilities:



\- vulnerability analysis

\- secure coding

\- risk assessment





\### Operations Layer



\- devops agent

\- release agent



Responsibilities:



\- automation

\- CI/CD

\- deployment validation





\### Knowledge Layer



\- documentation agent

\- knowledge agent



Responsibilities:



\- documentation management

\- architectural memory

\- ADR maintenance



\## Governance Workflow



Every significant change follows:



1\. Architecture analysis

2\. Implementation

3\. Testing

4\. Security validation

5\. Code review

6\. Documentation update

7\. Release validation





\## Consequences



Positive:



\- predictable AI collaboration

\- improved maintainability

\- stronger security posture

\- preserved architectural knowledge

\- scalable AI agent ecosystem





Negative:



\- additional validation steps

\- higher initial complexity

\- need for continuous governance maintenance





\## Future Evolution



Future improvements may include:



\- automated agent scoring

\- AI decision tracing

\- dependency graph analysis

\- compliance automation

\- production change approval workflows
